topic: claude code desktop ssh key vulnerability
headline_marked: [[Claude Code Desktop's Preview Could Read Your SSH Keys]] via HTML files over 256KB
headline: Claude Code Desktop's Preview Could Read Your SSH Keys via HTML files over 256KB
summary: A critical vulnerability allowed scripts in HTML preview files over 256KB to bypass security and steal sensitive credentials like SSH keys and AWS tokens. The flaw was patched on August 17, 2026, in Claude Desktop version 1.30096.1.
details: A critical vulnerability in Claude Code Desktop's HTML preview pane allowed scripts hidden in large HTML files to steal sensitive credentials. This included SSH private keys, AWS credentials, and GitHub tokens, which could then be sent to an attacker's server.

The flaw, dubbed 'SneakPeek' by Noma Security, was present in the app's preview functionality, not the AI model itself. It exploited a size-based branching logic where HTML files over 256KB bypassed crucial security protections like Content Security Policy (CSP) and opaque origins.

Anthropic, the developer of Claude, rated the bug CVSS v4.0 8.7 (High), treating its impact as equivalent to code execution. The issue was fixed via an auto-update in Claude Desktop version 1.30096.1, which shipped on August 17, 2026.

Users are advised to confirm their Claude Desktop app is updated to version 1.30096.1 or later. This vulnerability highlights the risk of previewing untrusted HTML files, even if they appear innocuous like coverage reports.

To mitigate similar risks, experts recommend using scoped, short-lived tokens instead of long-lived credentials on developer machines. Monitoring file reads and outbound connections at the runtime layer can also help detect suspicious activity.

The core lesson from this bug is to ensure consistent security checks across all code paths, especially those handling large inputs. Relying on size-based thresholds for security boundaries can create critical bypasses.

topic: ai overview sources not on google first page
headline_marked: [[29.8% of AI Overview sources don't appear]] in Google's first page at all
headline: 29.8% of AI Overview sources don't appear in Google's first page at all
summary: A new study reveals nearly a third of Google AI Overview citations come from pages not found on the first page of organic search results, indicating a distinct sourcing method.
details: A new study reveals that 29.8% of sources cited in Google's AI Overviews do not appear on the first page of organic search results. This finding challenges the assumption that AI Overviews simply pull from top-ranking pages.

Researchers at Washington University in St. Louis analyzed 55,393 Google searches over 40 days in early 2026. They collected AI Overviews, their citations, first-page results, and the content of cited webpages.

Google's own documentation explains this through "query fan-out," where the AI model splits queries into multiple related sub-queries. This allows it to retrieve and cite pages that don't rank for the primary query but answer a related sub-question.

Independent analyses confirm this trend: Ahrefs found only 38% of cited pages in the organic top 10 (down from 76% in July 2025), while BrightEdge reported a 17% overlap. The link between organic ranking and AI citation is weakening.

The study also found that AI Overview-cited domains received higher average credibility scores than traditional first-page results. Credibility was measured by domain authority, content quality, and trust signals, not just markup.

The researchers also noted an 11% error rate, where cited sources did not fully support the AI's claims. This is an upper limit, as dynamic content like Reddit threads and YouTube videos were hard to fully capture.

For content creators, the data suggests optimizing for breadth and specificity across related topics is more crucial than a single keyword ranking. Question-form queries are also significantly more likely to trigger an AI Overview.

The focus should shift from traditional SEO tactics like keyword stuffing and Schema density to producing credible, original research, first-hand experience, and expert analysis. This "non-commodity content" is what the AI prioritizes.
